name: Tilburg University
summary: Campus university in Tilburg for economics, business, law and social sciences; 14 English-taught bachelor's, including a liberal arts college.

ib.text: Full IB Diploma, 24+ points, three HL subjects; your school grades are assessed, not predictions. An English-taught IB exempts you from a test. Maths AA HL for Econometrics; AA SL/HL or AI HL for economics and business.

dates.label: Complete application deadline for non-EEA nationals, 23:59 CET
Complete application deadline for EEA nationals, 23:59 CET

programmes.name: Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL.
programmes.about: How intelligent systems work and how they relate to the human brain: programming, machine learning and deep learning, human-robot interaction and cognitive neuroscience, with labs for brain and behaviour and AI robotics.
programmes.overview: You study how intelligent systems work and how that relates to the human brain, starting with introductory AI, human cognition and programming. Year two adds machine learning, deep learning, human-computer and human-robot interaction, cognitive neuroscience and research experience, with practicals in the Brain and Behavior Lab. Ethics is built into the courses, and teaching is hands-on. In year three you take specialisation courses such as Hybrid Intelligence, use a mobility window for a minor, an internship or other courses, and write a bachelor's thesis. After a master's, graduates work as intelligent software developers, technology consultants, AI researchers or machine learning engineers.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink and upload your documents by 1 May; a matching activity follows.

programmes.name: Digital Culture and Society
programmes.ib: Non-EEA applicants also have until 1 May.
programmes.about: Digital culture and media in a globalised world: online identities, communities and social media, with strong training in writing; students publish on the programme's own online magazine, Diggit.
programmes.overview: You study digital culture, identity, community and the role of art in society, while building academic writing and research skills. Writing is central: students publish papers and opinion pieces on an online platform with a global readership, alongside search engine optimisation skills. Courses include Exploring Digital Cultures, Digital Media and Politics, and Art and Media in a Digital Society. In year two you choose electives or an internship, and in year three you build a profile with a minor, electives or an exchange and write a thesis. After a master's, graduates work in digital agencies, online journalism, cultural heritage, government and research, as editors, content coordinators or policy officers.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink and upload your documents by 1 May; a matching activity follows.

programmes.name: Double Bachelor: International Business Administration and Economics
programmes.ib: Two BSc degrees in four years: apply to both IBA and Economics, then opt in. Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL.
programmes.about: Two bachelor's degrees in four years: international business and economics integrated from the first semester to the thesis, combining strategy and management with economic modelling, econometrics and data analysis.
programmes.overview: Two bachelor's degrees are combined in one integrated programme, with economics and international business taught side by side from the first semester to the thesis. Year one covers micro- and macroeconomics, marketing, human resources, statistics and programming; later years add finance, strategy, international trade, economic growth, corporate governance, supply chain management, ethics and the effects of technology and data on business. In year four you choose electives, a semester abroad or an internship, and write a thesis in the discipline of your choice. Typical courses include International Finance, Welfare Economics and Comparative and Cross-Cultural Management.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the IBA and Economics requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May; the matching step after conditional admission is mandatory.

programmes.name: Economics
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL.
programmes.about: How choices by people, firms and governments shape the economy, studied with economic models and data applied to inequality, growth and climate change, in a small international programme with an optional semester abroad.
programmes.overview: You learn how people, firms and governments decide and how those decisions shape whole economies, using economic models and data. Year one builds the micro- and macroeconomic foundation with mathematics and statistics as tools; year two goes deeper into both and adds courses such as Development Economics and International Trade. In year three you can study a semester abroad, do an internship, or stay for minors in economics and business and electives, then write a thesis. Typical courses include Welfare Economics and International Finance. Graduates work as economists or data analysts in international organisations, banks, multinationals and research centres.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May; the matching step after conditional admission is mandatory.

programmes.name: Econometrics and Operations Research
programmes.about: Mathematical and statistical models for real decisions in business, finance and the public sector, from hospital planning to product flows, with an Improving Society Lab running alongside the first year.
programmes.overview: The first year pairs mathematics and statistics courses with economics and business courses, and runs alongside the Improving Society Lab, where you apply econometrics to real problems such as optimising medical treatment or distributing humanitarian aid. From year two you add asset pricing, stochastic operations research models and communication skills. In year three you specialise in one of the three main fields of econometrics, and can spend six months on exchange abroad, and the programme closes with a bachelor's thesis. After a master's, graduates work as supply chain specialists, quantitative analysts or business intelligence specialists.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements, including Maths AA HL, and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink and upload your documents by 1 May.

programmes.name: Entrepreneurship and Business Innovation
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL. Matching: interview an entrepreneur and compare them with one whose biography you read.
programmes.about: How new ideas become businesses: entrepreneurship and innovation with economics, finance, law and ethics, plus hands-on Entrepreneurship in Action projects every year.
programmes.overview: Courses in entrepreneurship, business innovation, business fundamentals and statistics run alongside the Entrepreneurship in Action series, in which you apply entrepreneurial methods in real projects. Year one has two such projects, one on exploring opportunities and one on building solutions. Year two covers law, finance, leadership and ethics, creative problem-solving, and entrepreneurship in start-ups, established companies and social ventures. In year three you can study abroad, do an internship or take a minor, then choose a specialisation course and finish with a graduation project. Many graduates start their own company or join a start-up, or go on to a master's.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May; the matching assignment (interviewing an entrepreneur) is mandatory.

programmes.name: Global Law
programmes.about: A full legal training (contract, tort, criminal, constitutional law) that looks beyond one legal system, comparing jurisdictions and tackling global problems such as digital technology and decolonisation. Awards an LLB.
programmes.overview: The programme covers the traditional legal subjects, such as contract, tort, criminal, administrative, property and constitutional law, but compares different legal systems rather than one. Year one introduces law, justice and legal history, with interdisciplinary work alongside economists and sociologists. From year two the focus moves to legal courses, including EU law and public international law. In year three you can go on exchange or stay for minors, and you write a thesis; typical courses include Business for Lawyers and Law, Technology and Society. After a master's, graduates work as consultants, legal advisers or compliance analysts, with alumni at NATO, the European Parliament and the International Criminal Court.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May; the matching step after conditional admission is mandatory.

programmes.name: Global Management of Social Issues
programmes.about: Societal problems such as poverty and migration approached from organisations: management, HR studies and sociology combined, with simulations like a humanitarian emergency response team.
programmes.overview: You tackle complex 'wicked problems' such as poverty, migration, climate change and humanitarian emergencies from an organisational and management angle, combining organisation and management studies, human resource studies and sociology. Year one adds social psychology, and year two brings philosophy and international law plus a simulation in which you join a humanitarian emergency response team. Courses include Wicked Problems 101, International Organizations and Advanced Project Management. In year three you do a project internship with an internationally active organisation, an exchange abroad or minors, and write a bachelor's thesis.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink and upload your documents by 1 May; a matching activity follows.

programmes.name: Human Resource Studies: People Management
programmes.about: The human side of organisations: wellbeing, inclusion, team performance and strategic people management, through psychology, sociology, economics and management, with HR analytics and consulting skills.
programmes.overview: The programme has an international slant with an emphasis on Europe, and links to large international companies. Year one introduces psychology, sociology, economics and management studies and starts applying them to work, organisations and people management. Year two combines these perspectives on strategic, financial and managerial aspects of HR, employee development, health and wellbeing, and teaches you to advise organisations on people policy. In year three you explore people management in an international setting and use a mobility window to study abroad, do an internship or take a minor, before writing a bachelor's thesis. Typical courses include Strategic HRM, Talent Management and Cross Cultural HRM.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink and upload your documents by 1 May; a matching activity follows.

programmes.name: International Business Administration
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL.
programmes.about: How international companies run and how culture shapes business: a broad base in economics, culture and leadership, with much training in writing, presenting and research among 50+ nationalities.
programmes.overview: The programme looks at how a large global organisation is run and how it relates to the world around it. Year one covers finance and investment, international strategy, human resource management, marketing, mathematics, statistics and programming, plus how AI and data change business. Year two adds management accounting, global sustainable leadership, cross-cultural management and ethics. In year three you specialise through a minor, a semester abroad or an internship, and write a thesis in a business discipline. After a master's, graduates work as consultants, supply chain managers or business analysts, with alumni at firms such as PwC, ASML and ABN AMRO.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May; the matching step after conditional admission is mandatory.

programmes.name: International Sociology
programmes.about: What makes societies differ and what connects them: migration, cultural difference, poverty and inequality, linked to policy, with a second-year choice between culture and social-risk specialisations.
programmes.overview: You study society from a comparative perspective on the Western world, and carry out a sociological research project every year. Year one introduces sociology alongside political science, social psychology and research methods. In year two you choose a specialisation, either Culture in Comparative Perspective or Social Risks in a Changing World, and finish the year with a research project in that field. Year three leaves room for minors, electives, study abroad or an internship, and you write a thesis in your specialisation. After a master's, graduates work as sociology teachers or journalists, and alumni have joined ministries, research agencies, newspapers and companies such as ING and Philips.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink and upload your documents by 1 May; a matching activity follows.

programmes.name: Psychology
programmes.ib: Numerus fixus, 250 English-track places: apply in Studielink by 15 January 2027 and complete your file by 31 January. Knowledge test 60%, grades 40%.
programmes.about: The mind and behaviour, with a flexible curriculum of nine majors, including economic, forensic and medical psychology, combined with a minor of your choice.
programmes.overview: You build a foundation across all areas of psychology in year one, along with academic skills and research methods. In year two you pick one of nine majors, among them clinical, forensic, developmental, economic, social, and work and organisational psychology, and take statistics, specialisation courses and supervised small-group research. Year three finishes the major with a professional practice course, a minor, two electives and a bachelor's thesis, and you can study abroad for six months. Teaching combines lectures with lab research, tutorials and group assignments. Typical courses include Brain and Behavior and Personality Psychology.
programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: 250 English-track places. Apply by 15 Jan 2027; ranked on an online knowledge test in March (60%) and your grades (40%), plus a motivation assignment.

programmes.name: Theology
programmes.ib: Matching: a short essay, discussed at a matching interview.
programmes.about: Faith and reason, ethics and meaning, and religion's role in society, taught in a small community; the Tilburg School of Catholic Theology can award canonical degrees recognised by the Holy See.
programmes.overview: The programme spans fields from biblical studies to spirituality, using history, philosophy, literature and the social sciences to reflect on questions of meaning, identity, tradition and values. Year one maps the main fields of theology and introduces Greek and Hebrew; year two goes deeper and adds Latin. Courses include Comparative Religion, on Islam, Buddhism and Hinduism, Systematic Philosophy, and reading the Bible in its original languages. Year three opens a semester mobility window for electives, other programmes or courses abroad, and ends with a bachelor's thesis on a topic of your choice.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply by 1 May; a short essay is discussed at a matching conversation.

programmes.name: University College Tilburg: Liberal Arts and Sciences
programmes.ib: Selective: application form with a short essay, then an interview. Majors: Interdisciplinary Social Sciences, Cognitive Neuroscience and Behavior, or Law, Politics, and Culture.
programmes.about: A small interdisciplinary college where you design your own path through philosophy, law, sociology, psychology, neuroscience, politics and economics, then major in social sciences, cognitive neuroscience or law, politics and culture.
programmes.overview: A broad first year of core courses and academic skills leads to a choice of major: Law, Politics and Culture; Cognitive Neuroscience and Behavior; Interdisciplinary Social Sciences; or Design and Technology. From year two you link your major to a theme shared across majors: Transformations to Sustainability, Democracy and Justice, or Technology and Society, and apply knowledge to real-world problems. In year three you take a minor or exchange abroad and complete two final projects: a bachelor's thesis and a Societal Capstone applying your knowledge to real-life projects. Courses include Evil, Public Law and Democracy, and Brain and Behavior, in small classes.
programmes.selectionNote: Selective: after the eligibility check you send an application form with a short essay, then have a mandatory interview. EEA deadline 15 June.

notes: Binding study advice: 42 of 60 first-year credits (EC) to continue; Psychology, Econometrics and Liberal Arts and Sciences are piloting a non-binding advice from 2026-27.
Applicants with a non-Dutch diploma, IB included, pay a one-time €100 application fee; some programmes, such as Economics and IBA, then make a matching step mandatory.
Data Science (joint with TU/e) is applied for only via TU/e, and Leisure Studies via Breda University of Applied Sciences, though both appear in Tilburg's list.
